note_on_method: Each venue page rests on the City of Tampa's pickleball page, one card per venue with a label, a name, an address and a count, dated "Updated: 10/28/2025", and, where the address is also a community centre, on the City's recreation-centres list for the phone number and the "Features:" line. The US Census address geocoder and OpenStreetMap supply the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Four outdoor pickleball courts in East Tampa, on a card the City writes in three lines: "Al Barnes Park / 2902 N 32nd St, Tampa, 33605 / 4 courts", under the label "Outdoor Pickleball". That is the entire published record of pickleball at this park: no hours, no session, no note, just an address and a number.

Four courts is a workable number: two games at once, or a group of eight rotating without much waiting. The park has no entry on the City's recreation-centres list, so no building, gym or phone number is attached to the address. The pickleball page names a contact for the whole programme, a Site Supervisor at 59 Columbia Drive, 813-712-0321, and that is the nearest thing to a phone number Al Barnes has.
slots.getting_there:
2902 N 32nd St, Tampa, FL 33605. The address is the City's, and it resolves through OpenStreetMap rather than the US Census address file, which holds no record of it. OpenStreetMap matches it at house-number level on North 32nd Street, in the East Ybor area, in Hillsborough County and inside the incorporated city of Tampa.

The City publishes nothing about parking at this park, nothing about restrooms, and nothing about how to reach it by any means.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts, outdoors, and a City record that stops there. Hours are not stated, so there is no way to say whether the park closes at sunset. Lighting is not stated, so evening play is an open question rather than a yes or a no. Price and surface are not stated either.

With no published open-play time, nothing on the City's record suggests a rotation forms here on its own, so bring a group. Four courts is enough for two games and a short wait.

faqs.a: Four, on the City's card: "Al Barnes Park / 2902 N 32nd St, Tampa, 33605 / 4 courts", under the label "Outdoor Pickleball".
Not stated. The City says nothing about lighting at this or any Tampa venue, so it is recorded as not stated rather than as a no.
Not stated. Only Madison Street Park, Vila Brothers Park and the New Tampa Sports Pavilion carry hours on the City's pickleball page; Al Barnes does not.

slots.description:
Four outdoor pickleball courts at Copeland Park in north Tampa, from a card that reads "Copeland Park / 11001 N 15th St., 33612 / 4 courts" under "Outdoor Pickleball". The same address appears a second time in City records: the recreation-centres page lists the Copeland Park Center at 11001 N 15th St, 33612, with a phone number, 813-975-2743, and a features line of "Computer Lab, Fitness Room, Gymnasium, Pool Facility, After School, Summer Camp, Stay & Play, Contracted Instructor (Urban Line Dance)".

So there is a building with a gymnasium at this address, and the City does not list indoor pickleball in it. The four pickleball courts are outdoor courts on the City's own label, and the gym is a fact about the building rather than about them.
slots.getting_there:
11001 N 15th St, Tampa, FL 33612. The US Census address geocoder matched the address exactly as the City writes it, at house-number level, and placed it in Hillsborough County inside the incorporated place Tampa city.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms at the park. The recreation-centres page does give the Copeland Park Center a phone number, 813-975-2743, which is the only published way to ask a question about this address.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four outdoor courts with no stated hours, no stated lighting, no stated price and no stated surface. The card carries a count and an address and nothing else.

What the recreation-centres page adds is that the same address holds a staffed centre with a gymnasium, a fitness room and a pool, running after-school and summer-camp programmes. That tells you the site is in use for other things through the school year and the summer, without telling you anything about the courts. With four courts and no published session, expect to bring your own game.

faqs.a: Four outdoor courts, on the City's card: "Copeland Park / 11001 N 15th St., 33612 / 4 courts".

faqs.q: Is there indoor pickleball at Copeland?
faqs.a: Not on the City's record. The Copeland Park Center at the same address has a gymnasium on the recreation-centres list, but the City lists no indoor pickleball courts there.
Not stated. The City says nothing about lighting at this or any other Tampa venue, so it is recorded as not stated.

slots.description:
Six outdoor pickleball courts, and the only outdoor card in Tampa that names a session. The City writes it as "Cuscaden Park / 2900 N 15th St., 33605 / Senior open play Wed 9-11 am / 6 courts" under "Outdoor Pickleball". That middle line is the one scheduled pickleball time the City publishes for any outdoor park in the city: two hours on a Wednesday morning, for seniors, on these courts. Outside it the City says nothing about who plays here or when.

Six courts is the joint second-largest outdoor count published in Tampa, level with Julian B Lane Riverfront Park and behind only Macfarlane's eight, and it is enough for a rotation rather than a single game. Cuscaden has no entry on the recreation-centres list, so there is no building or centre phone number attached to the address.
slots.getting_there:

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms here. The pickleball page's contact for the whole programme is a Site Supervisor at 59 Columbia Drive, 813-712-0321.
slots.what_to_expect:
Six outdoor courts and one published fact about their use: senior open play on Wednesday mornings, 9 to 11 am. For a senior player that is the one time in Tampa the City has put in writing that a game will be there when you arrive. For everyone else it is two hours on a Wednesday when the courts are spoken for.

Hours are not stated, so the closing time is unknown. Lighting, price and surface are not stated. Six courts is the number at which turning up alone starts to be reasonable, though the City publishes no open-play time except the senior one.

Wednesdays, 9 to 11 am, on the City's card. It is the only scheduled outdoor pickleball session the City publishes anywhere in Tampa.
Not stated, apart from the senior session. The City gives no opening or closing time for this park.

slots.description:
Two outdoor courts on Davis Islands that the City calls "2 multi-purpose courts", and this page keeps the City's word. The card reads "Davis Islands / 155 Columbia Drive, Tampa, 33606 / 2 multi-purpose courts" under the label "Outdoor pickleball". A multi-purpose court is one that may be lined or set up for something other than pickleball when you get there. The City lists it as a pickleball venue all the same, counts two, and says nothing about what else the courts are for.

The address is a few doors along Columbia Drive from number 59, which the pickleball page names as its contact address, the office of Site Supervisor Andrew Sheets, and which the City's recreation-centres list gives as the Sandra Freedman Complex, "Features: Tennis Complex". Two courts is a game, not a rotation.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms. It does publish two phone numbers on the same street: the programme contact at 59 Columbia Drive, 813-712-0321, and the Sandra Freedman Complex at the same number, 813-259-1664. Neither is described as the courts' own.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two multi-purpose courts, outdoors, with nothing else stated. Two courts is a game, not a rotation: a group of four can play, a group of eight will wait. Multi-purpose means you should be ready to find the courts in use for something else, or lined for it. Hours, lighting, price and surface are not stated.

With the City's programme office on the same street, the sensible move before a trip for these two courts alone is to ring 813-712-0321 and ask what they are set up for this week.

The City does not say. It lists the venue under outdoor pickleball and counts two courts; what else they are lined or set up for is not stated.
The pickleball page's contact is a Site Supervisor at 59 Columbia Drive, 813-712-0321, a few doors from the courts. It is the programme's number, not the courts' own.

slots.description:
Two outdoor courts and two indoor courts at one address in north Tampa, published here as one venue with four. The City writes them as two cards. Under "Outdoor Pickleball": "Forest Hills / 724 W 109th Ave., 33612 / 2 courts". Under "Indoor Pickleball": "Forest Hills Community Center / 724 W 109th Ave, 33612 / 2 courts / Play resumes after Summer Camp ends / Monday, 10 am-12:30 pm / Wednesday, 10 am-1 pm / Friday, 6-7:30 pm". Same address, two counts, and both are printed so the sum can be checked.

The building is on the City's recreation-centres list as the Forest Hills Center, 813-931-2105, "Features: Computer Lab, Fitness Room, Gymnasium, After School, Summer Camp, Contracted Instructor (Shotokan Karate)", so the indoor courts are in a centre with a gymnasium, and the summer camp the card mentions is a programme the City runs in that building.
slots.getting_there:
724 W 109th Ave, Tampa, FL 33612. The US Census address geocoder matched the address as the City writes it, at house-number level, in Hillsborough County inside Tampa city.

The City publishes nothing about parking. The centre has a phone number, 813-931-2105, on the recreation-centres page, and for a venue whose indoor sessions are suspended during summer camp that is the number to ring before an evening trip.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two kinds of court and two kinds of record. Outdoors, two courts with no stated hours, lighting, price or surface. Indoors, two courts in the centre with a session schedule: Monday 10 am to 12:30 pm, Wednesday 10 am to 1 pm, Friday 6 to 7:30 pm, and a note that "Play resumes after Summer Camp ends".

The City's page is dated 28 October 2025 and the note carries no year, so it is printed as the City printed it. Two indoor courts at fixed times is a session, not a drop-in facility: outside those hours the gym is the centre's, not the pickleball players'.

The Highland Pines Center at the address runs after-school and summer programmes, so the site is used through the year for things other than pickleball, and the City does not say whether the courts are affected. This is a bring-your-own-game venue on the City's record.

slots.description:
Six outdoor pickleball courts at Julian B Lane Riverfront Park, and the six is the City's own arithmetic. The card reads "Julian B Lane Riverfront Park / 1001 N Boulevard, 33606 / 2 permanent courts / 4 portable net courts" under "Outdoor Pickleball". Two courts stand with their nets; four more are laid out for nets that are brought out, and the City counts them. Both figures are printed here so the sum can be checked, and the distinction matters on the ground: two courts are certain, four depend on the portable nets being there.

Julian B Lane is one of the parks the City names under "Featured Parks" in its site navigation. The venue is marked for a re-check at the next cadence because the count changed from two to six.

The resolver's postcode publishes and the difference is stated rather than hidden; the street and number are the City's.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms at this park.
slots.what_to_expect:
Six courts on paper: two you can rely on and four that need nets. That is what "2 permanent courts / 4 portable net courts" means for a player. If the portable nets are out, six courts is a rotation; if they are not, two courts is a game.

The City says nothing about when or whether the nets are out, nothing about hours, lighting, price or surface. The courts are outdoor on the City's label. Bring a net if you have one and want the four; the City does not say who supplies them.

The City's page lists one other eight-court venue, Rowlett Park, and that one is not published here because its address, "2401 E Yukon St.", is found by neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap.

Eight courts is enough for a rotation to form and keep moving, which makes this the Tampa venue where turning up without a group is the most reasonable plan, on the count alone. The City writes nothing else on the card: no hours, no session, no note. Macfarlane has no entry on the recreation-centres list, so there is no building, gym or centre phone number attached to the address.

slots.description:
One outdoor pickleball court east of downtown, and one of only two outdoor Tampa cards that state hours. The City writes "Madison Street Park / 1224 E Madison St., 33602 / Open daily from sunrise to sunset / 1 court" under "Outdoor Pickleball". One court is a game, not a rotation, and this is the smallest published venue in the city.

Of Tampa's twelve outdoor venues, only this park and Vila Brothers Park carry "Open daily from sunrise to sunset", and the New Tampa Sports Pavilion carries facility hours. The other nine say nothing. OpenStreetMap places the address in the Ybor City area. The park has no entry on the City's recreation-centres list, so the card is the whole of the published record.

slots.what_to_expect:
One court, open sunrise to sunset, outdoors. That is a complete description of what the City states, and it means a single game at a time, in daylight, with no published lighting to extend it and no published price to pay. Surface is not stated.

With one court there is no rotation to join and no second game to wait for, so this is a venue for a pair or a four who arrive together, and if someone is already on it there is nowhere else at this address to go. The sunrise-to-sunset line is the City's and it is the one hard planning fact here.

The City labels the pickleball courts outdoor and this page follows the label; nothing on either page says the courts are under the pavilion roof.

sources.evidence: All sixteen published addresses matched at house-number level and were placed in Hillsborough County, FL, inside the incorporated place Tampa. Ten resolved through the Census address file as the City writes them: Copeland, Cuscaden, Davis Islands, Forest Hills, Macfarlane, New Tampa Sports Pavilion, Vila Brothers, David M Barksdale (in 33607 against the pickleball page's 33606), Loretta Ingraham and Port Tampa. Four resolved through OpenStreetMap: Al Barnes Park and Julian B Lane Riverfront Park because the Census file holds no record of the address (Julian B Lane in 33607 against the City's 33606); Madison Street Park because the Census answered "1224 MADISON ST", dropping the East; Cordelia B Hunt Center because the Census answered "4602 S HIMES AVE, TAMPA, FL, 33611", flipping the direction and the postcode. Highland Pines Park stands on the Census answer "4505 E 21ST AVE" and Skyview Park on "6203 MARTINDALE AVE", because OpenStreetMap holds nothing for the City's spelling and there is one street under one name in each case. "2401 E Yukon St." (Rowlett Park) is found by neither resolver; "4700 S Clark Ave., 33611" (Foster Park) is answered by the Census as "4700 N CLARK AVE, 33614" and not found by OpenStreetMap.
